reference: GNU coreutils dirname, invoked from the reference side's PATH. The input/output cases follow POSIX dirname pathname processing; the option case checks GNU's documented --zero option. The Bash type/help case is an independent metadata contract based on the dirname builtin's published synopsis and short documentation.
coverage: empty operand and ordinary dot components
relative paths containing dot-dot components without canonicalization
option terminator with a dash-leading operand
missing operand status and diagnostic presence
Bash builtin type and short-help metadata
exclusions: No deferred cases: dirname performs bounded pathname-string processing, and the GNU reference is available in the fixture environment.
Long path limits, every GNU diagnostic wording, locale-specific diagnostics, and all option permutations are not exhaustively covered.

cases.purpose: Check the directory portion of a three-component relative pathname.
Check that a name without a slash and an empty operand both map to the current-directory marker.
Check removal of trailing slashes and trimming of repeated separators immediately before the final component, while preserving repeated separators inside the resulting directory name.
cases.script: for path in 'one/two///' 'one//two///' 'one//two//three///'; do dirname "$path"; done

cases.purpose: Check all-slash operands, the root pathname, and a top-level absolute component.
cases.script: for path in '/' '////' '/leaf'; do dirname "$path"; done

cases.purpose: Check that dirname removes only the final component and does not canonicalize dot-dot components.
Check that -- ends option parsing so a dash-leading pathname is treated as the operand.
Check GNU's missing-operand exit status and ensure both implementations report the usage error; the failure is explicitly captured before the fixture returns it.
Check GNU dirname's --zero option, which emits a NUL terminator instead of a newline and may reveal an option-support compatibility difference in the loadable.
Check Bash metadata without invoking dirname: type reports a builtin and short help matches the dirname builtin's documented short description.
cases.script: kind=$(type -t dirname); summary=$(help -d dirname); [[ $kind == builtin ]] || exit 1; [[ $summary == 'dirname - Display directory portion of pathname.' ]] || exit 1; printf 'builtin\nhelp-summary-ok\n'
